invariants.text: Task and event history is append-only (`loom_events`); tasks carry input/output hashes and checkpoints and resume after a crash — invariant
Raw sources are immutable: content-addressed blobs (`blobs/ab/cd/<sha256>`, chmod 444), with sources and provenance rows for every import — invariant
Możliwy explicit override usera zawsze wygrywa, o ile nie łamie twardego safety/invariant contract.
C ABI: opaque context, caller-freed JSON strings, error object, negative codes — invariant (versioned by `LOOM_ABI_VERSION`)
`items` — Typed items: `idea`, `decision`, `rejected_option`, `open_question`, `implementation`, `bug`, `requirement`, `invariant`, `rationale`.
Shared on-disk format with the Python app (schema v4 DDL, IDs, timestamps, `json.dumps` formatting, file names, data-dir resolution) — invariant

Following constitution A of the architecture document, each decision is one of: **invariant** (enforced in code and tests), **policy/default** (data you can replace) or **platform detail** (an adapter).
FTS is derived, rebuildable state with a LIKE fallback — invariant; whether FTS5 is available is a platform detail
Loom state only in `loom_*` tables; no triggers or virtual tables in the main DB — invariant
Errors are values (`Result`/`Status`); nothing throws across the C ABI — invariant
**invariant** — musi być w kodzie/kontrakcie,

invariants.text: Secrets and passwords are read from stdin (with echo off on a terminal) and never accepted as arguments.
The output directory gets a `.loom-archive` marker, and the walker skips marked directories so a run never ingests its own output.

`LoomBridge` is added to exactly one `WebView`, which only ever navigates within that virtual origin — `shouldOverrideUrlLoading` hands any other host to the system browser instead of navigating the WebView there — so the interface is neve…
Loom reconciles it after writes from any process and rebuilds it when it is missing or corrupt, so the main database never needs an SQLite build with FTS5.

invariants.text: Sources and tests are picked up by glob, so adding a file never requires editing `CMakeLists.txt`.
On failure, JSON functions return `{"error":{"code":"not_found","message":"..."}}` and never NULL (except `loom_init`).
**Never run on a device or emulator** — no Android SDK/NDK in this environment.
`loom/CMakeLists.txt`'s `LOOM_WITH_OPENSSL` is forced `OFF` for this build (`app/src/main/cpp/CMakeLists.txt`): the native library never links cpp-httplib/OpenSSL.

invariants.text: Config defaults = Python `DEFAULTS`; Loom policy keys (`loom_event_log_types`, `loom_task_workers`) are served as fallbacks and never written — policy/default

decisions.text: Provider manifests and capabilities; `can(resource, capability, constraints)` instead of `if provider == X` — policy/default
Context budget (tokens ≈ code points / 4), source order memory → graph → FTS — policy/default
Relation vocabulary (inverse, symmetry, category); unknown types auto-registered — policy/default (seeded JSON)
The C ABI returns parsed JSON for metadata columns.
Unicode tables pinned to the generating CPython (currently Unicode 14.0) — platform detail (regenerate with `tools/gen_unicode_tables.py`)
Row ordering breaks ties by `rowid`, so batch-imported rows come back in insertion order.
System SQLite vs vendored amalgamation — platform detail
Bad JSON in a column is returned as a string instead of raising.
Log sinks (stderr, ring buffer, logcat through the C ABI) — platform detail
Native TF-IDF is always available, so the default selector tier is 2.
`update_msg` enforces the status whitelist.
JSON as the ABI codec (`nlohmann::ordered_json`, which keeps key order like Python dicts) — platform detail; the semantics live in the C++ types
Analyzer rules (regexes, topic keywords), generated from `core/semantic.py` — policy/default (data)
`estimate_cost` parses string prices.
HTTP stack (cpp-httplib + OpenSSL, or an injected platform transport) — platform detail
`ChatEngine` no longer sends the new user message twice.
Każda arbitralna decyzja pozostaje otwarta, dopóki nie wymusza jej kontrakt, test, koszt lub ograniczenie platformy.
Nie nadajemy teraz nowej nazwy całemu ekosystemowi — to decyzja kosmetyczna i nie jest potrzebna do implementacji.
Nie wybieramy jeszcze pełnego roadmapu produktu.
Nie wybieramy „YAML” jako fundamentu.

Nie budujemy pięciu projektów: „ChatADHD”, „Loom”, „autonomiczny agent”, „analizator archiwów”, „multi-LLM knowledge graph chatbot”.

If `loom-server` ends up with its own lightweight health-check mode this can be dropped in favour of `CMD ["/app/loom-server", "--healthcheck"]` (JSON form, no shell needed) — worth revisiting once that binary exists.
`timeline` — Chronological path per theme, ChatGPT/Claude forks (kept or abandoned branch), version groups, commits.
**Tak jako jeden z formatów authoringu; nie jako „prawda systemu”.**
